question.text: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, the minimum price for a preferential issue of frequently traded shares is the higher of the volume weighted average prices (VWAP) of the related equity shares on a recognised stock exchange over which two lookback periods preceding the relevant date?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI ICDR Regulations, the floor price for a preferential issue of frequently traded shares is the higher of (a) the 90 trading days VWAP and (b) the 10 trading days VWAP of the related equity shares on a recognised stock exchange preceding the relevant date. If the Articles of Association prescribe a method that yields a higher floor, that prevails. The Trap: The "26 weeks and 2 weeks" formulation reflects an earlier version of the rule and is no longer the test set out in the current ICDR text. "240 trading days" is the lookback used to define a "frequently traded share" (turnover threshold), not the pricing lookback. Cross-Exam Context: NISM Series IX (Merchant Banking) tests preferential issue pricing extensively. NISM Series XV (Research Analyst) covers it when analyzing dilution impact. Analyst's Pro-Tip: The "higher of two averages" rule means that in a falling market the 90-day average typically sets the floor, while in a rising market the 10-day average can be the binding constraint.
